summary.text: Mycelium is the root-like body of a fungus, made of a mass of branching, thread-like hyphae.
A fungus feeds through it: the hyphae release enzymes that break food down into smaller units, which are then absorbed.
Mycelium decomposes plant material, helps most plants absorb water and nutrients, and is used to make materials such as artificial leather.

facts.label: Largest colonies
facts.value: Can span thousands of acres, as in Armillaria

facts.label: Pollutant cleanup
facts.value: Mycoremediation breaks down pollutants such as petroleum

facts.label: Sound absorbed
facts.value: 70 to 75 percent at 1500 Hz or less

items.prompt: A lone fungal spore sprouts in a clean dish and grows a thread network by itself. Will mushrooms form there?

options.label: Yes, any single network forms them after a week
Yes, but only when the dish is dry
No, two compatible networks must first join
No, because mushrooms need sunlight to start

items.explain: A single spore grows monokaryotic mycelium, which cannot reproduce sexually. Mushrooms can form only after two compatible mycelia join into dikaryotic mycelium.

items.prompt: A fungus is growing on a fallen log. How does it feed?

options.label: It releases enzymes that break the wood into smaller units, then absorbs them
It swallows chunks of the wood whole and digests them inside
It draws sugar from sunlight through its thread-like body
It drills into the wood and sucks out sap like an insect

items.explain: Hyphae secrete enzymes that break biological polymers into smaller units such as monomers, which the mycelium then absorbs.

items.prompt: How does fungal mycelium around plant roots typically affect most plants?

options.label: It smothers the roots so they cannot take in oxygen
It replaces the roots so the plant stops growing its own
It feeds on the leaves until the plant dies
It increases how efficiently they absorb water and nutrients

items.explain: Mycelium of ectomycorrhizal and arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi increases the efficiency of water and nutrient absorption in most plants.

items.prompt: Petroleum has soaked into a patch of soil. How could fungi help?

options.label: They would turn the oil to sugar using sunlight
They may use its carbon-based molecules as food and so break it down
They would help only if killed first
They would cover it and block air without changing it

items.explain: Petroleum products are organic molecules and a potential carbon source for fungi, which can degrade them in a process called mycoremediation, unless the chemicals prove toxic.

items.prompt: A gardener turns a compost heap and sees web-like networks on decaying leaves. Why is that good news?

options.label: It means the compost has gone bad and must be thrown out
It shows weeds are rooting in the heap
It is a mold that must be killed before the heap can be used
Fungi are converting the material, including lignin that many other microbes cannot break down

items.explain: Fungi are essential for converting biomass into compost, since they decompose lignin, which many other composting microorganisms cannot. Turning a pile exposes their visible networks.

items.prompt: An architect likes grown mycelium bricks for being light and biodegradable. What drawback makes tall load-bearing use hard?

options.label: It releases toxic resins in a fire
On its own it resists being squeezed only weakly
It is too heavy for its strength
It cannot be shaped to a mold

items.explain: Mycelium does not have particularly high compressive strength on its own, which makes large-scale structural use difficult.
